item.title: Treat gunshot victims first; police report can wait – IGP Disu to doctors
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab The Inspector General of Police, Tunji Disu, has urged hospitals and healthcare workers across the country to treat gunshot victims immediately without demanding police reports, warning that delays could cost lives. Disu also called on members of the public to assist injured persons in accessing medical attention, assuring them that they would not face punishment for helping victims. The IGP made the appeal in a sensitisation message by the National Orientation Agency (NOA) in collaboration with the Nigeria Police Force, shared by the police on its X account on Thursday. Addressing Nigerians, police officers and medical personnel, Disu described the treatment of gunshot victims as a matter of life and death, stressing that no police documentation was required before emergency medical care could be provided. “Fellow Nigerians, I am here to address a matter of life and death – the treatment of gunshot victims in our hospitals. “To my fellow officers, to my medical personnel across the nation, and to every Nigerian listening, treating gunshot victims does not require a police report. “When a gunshot victim is brought to any hospital, the law does not require a police report before treatment,” he said. He urged doctors and other healthcare workers to prioritise saving lives rather than allow administrative procedures to delay emergency treatment. “To our doctors and healthcare workers, you are enjoined to treat gunshot victims immediately without waiting for a police report. Our duty is not to create fear but to protect lives. We wish to reassure citizens of their safety at all times,” Disu added. The police chief also appealed to Nigerians not to hesitate to help people who sustain gunshot injuries, emphasising that the law protects those who assist victims. “To the members of the public, if you see someone injured, do not hesitate to help. You will not be punished for helping. “Again, to my officers and medical personnel, please uphold the law because every second counts. Treat first, save lives,” he said. In a related message accompanying the video, the Nigeria Police Force warned that refusing or delaying medical attention for gunshot victims was punishable under the Compulsory Treatment and Care for Victims of Gunshots Act, 2017. According to the police, the legislation requires all public and private hospitals to provide immediate treatment to gunshot victims, regardless of whether they have police reports or clearance. The police further warned that violations of the Act could attract imprisonment of up to 15 years and other penalties, depending on the offence. The law provides that every hospital in Nigeria, whether public or private, must receive and provide immediate and adequate treatment to anyone with gunshot wounds, with or without police clearance. It also places a responsibility on members of the public, including security personnel, to assist victims and ensure they are taken to the nearest hospital for treatment

item.title: Burna Boy, Asake, Seyi Vibez feature on GTA VI soundtrack
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Nigerian music stars Burna Boy, Asake and Seyi Vibez have secured spots on the soundtrack of the highly anticipated video game, Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI). The Nigerian artistes are among several international performers featured on the game’s soundtrack, which was recently unveiled by Rockstar Games, the developer of the popular gaming franchise. Some of their songs will feature on AfroBank FM, an in-game radio station dedicated to African music, including Afrobeats, amapiano, African classics and 3-step sounds. Burna Boy is also set to co-host the station alongside British DJ and record producer Palms Trax, who appears in the game under the name Palmsy. Among the Nigerian tracks featured on the station are Asake’s ‘Joha’ and ‘Giza’, a collaboration between Burna Boy and Seyi Vibez. The station’s previewed playlist also includes ‘Gye Wani’ by Pat Thomas featuring Ebo Taylor, as well as ‘Shay’sana’ by DJ Lag and Robot Boii featuring Kamo Mphela. Burna Boy also makes a separate contribution to the game’s official soundtrack with his song ‘Bigger’. Other international artistes featured on the soundtrack include Travis Scott, Dua Lipa, Cardi B, Gunna, Young Thug, Kodak Black, Don Toliver, Zara Larsson, Camila Cabello and Lana Del Rey. The development marks another international gaming appearance for Nigerian music, as Afrobeats continues to gain visibility across global entertainment platforms. GTA VI is the latest instalment in Rockstar Games’ Grand Theft Auto series, one of the world’s most popular video game franchises. item.title: UDUS medical academics threaten five-day warning strike
item.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto The Nigerian Association of Medical and Dental Academics (NAMDA), Usmanu Danfodiyo University, Sokoto (UDUS)/Usmanu Danfodiyo University Teaching Hospital (UDUTH) Chapter, has threatened to embark on a five-day warning strike over alleged irregularities in salary payments, partial implementation of professional allowances and outstanding promotion arrears owed to its members. The association, at a press briefing in Sokoto on Thursday, said the unresolved welfare and remuneration issues had persisted despite several rounds of consultations, formal correspondence and peaceful engagements with the university management. It warned that its members might be left with no option but to embark on an indefinite strike if the issues were not addressed. Speaking at the briefing, presided over by Professor Usman Bello, NAMDA said its members had exercised considerable patience and goodwill through sustained dialogue with the relevant authorities, but expressed regret that the engagements had not produced the desired results. The association said its concerns centred on the continued partial implementation of professional allowances under the revised Consolidated Medical Salary Structure (CONMESS), unexplained salary disparities among members on the same grade levels and steps, and the non-payment of promotion arrears covering 2017 to 2024. It also alleged that some eligible members were excluded from the payment of 2025 and 2026 promotion arrears, describing the situation as an administrative and financial burden that had continued to affect the welfare and morale of medical academics. According to the association, comparable institutions in both Northern and Southern Nigeria had fully implemented the revised CONMESS, a development it said had heightened concerns among its members over disparities in remuneration. NAMDA recalled that it had pursued several avenues to resolve the dispute, including meetings with university authorities, submission of formal letters and supporting documents, and interventions by senior colleagues and elders. However, it said those efforts had yet to yield the desired outcome. The association also raised concerns over the migration of experienced medical professionals, including senior consultants and professors, to other countries in search of better working conditions. It described the development, popularly known as “japa”, as a threat to medical education and healthcare delivery in the country. “Mr President is aware of the ongoing exodus of highly experienced academic staff, including senior consultants and professors, to other countries, a trend popularly known as ‘japa’,” it said. NAMDA added that the Federal Government’s decision to increase the admission quota for medical students had placed additional pressure on the declining number of medical teachers. item.title: China, US, Russia issue ‘peace declaration’ after first summit
item.description: China, the United States and Russia issued a “peace declaration” Thursday following an unprecedented leaders’ summit, almost five years into the Ukraine war and with Donald Trump bogged down in Iran. The statement after Xi Jinping, Trump and Vladimir Putin met in China, said that they wanted to reform the United Nations, to protect diplomatic immunity and boost supply and production of refined petroleum products. “The three heads of state engaged in an in-depth exchange of views on the current international situation and committed themselves to upholding strategic stability and international security,” said the statement published by Chinese state media and the Kremlin, but not yet by the White House. The three-way meeting took place with Russia’s years-long offensive in Ukraine grinding on, mayhem in the Middle East in the wake of Trump’s attacks on Iran, and an ascendant China looking to strengthen its hand in East Asia. “Our countries have many converging interests when it comes to resolving regional conflicts, including, of course, the conflict in Ukraine,” Putin said at the start of the meeting, adding they had a “shared responsibility for maintaining international peace and security”. The three men made opening remarks touching on weighty topics from nuclear weapons to the war in Ukraine as they met around a large, dark round table with a pink flower arrangement at its centre. The discussion behind closed doors in Kylin Villa in Shenzhen ended after an hour and 20 minutes. Trump said the three men were “making history”, while Putin said they wrote a new “page in the history of diplomacy”. “The three countries share a common perspective on safeguarding world peace,” Xi said. ICC, UN and oil In their joint statement, the leaders agreed that “the International Criminal Court and other similar institutions must not abuse their jurisdiction.” Putin is subject to an ICC arrest warrant while Trump’s administration has vowed to dismantle the court “brick by brick”. The leaders also “acknowledged the vital importance of the principle of state consent and the respect for (diplomatic) immunity enjoyed by state officials”, the statement said, adding that each country was “committed” to advancing the reform of the United Nations. Putin said the discussion would also touch on food and energy security – both of which have been upended by conflicts in Iran and Ukraine. The joint statement said the countries “plan to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products”, reaffirming “the importance of the stable flow of energy”. The summit stoked fears that the three powerful men want to divide the globe into spheres of influence, for example by making decisions impacting Ukraine over the heads of Kyiv or Europe. item.title: FIFA chief Infantino faces challenge from France’s Diallo, Japan’s Tashima
item.description: French football chief Philippe Diallo and veteran Japanese official Kozo Tashima were on Thursday confirmed by FIFA as the challengers to incumbent Gianni Infantino in next year’s presidential election. Infantino has faced criticism over his aborted plan to allow private investment into the World Cup, but he retains considerable support for his bid to win re-election next March. French Football Federation president Diallo will represent UEFA, the European confederation which has been the most vocal in its criticism of Infantino. Tashima is a former head of the Japan Football Association and has served on the FIFA Council. FIFA said the candidacies will be examined by the body’s electoral committee before a final decision is made on whether to admit them. Ramon Vega, the Swiss former Tottenham defender who had expressed a desire to run against Infantino, was not included among the candidates. Diallo has indicated he would like to hold talks with Tashima, with a view to “joining forces” to unseat Infantino. The 68-year-old Japanese official, who has said he wants to make FIFA a “more trusted organisation”, said he was open to talks but was cautious about the steps after that. “It’s clear we need to talk,” Tashima told French sports daily L’Equipe on Wednesday. “But we must consider one thing: is the mere fact that our programmes are similar, enough for us to decide to work together, or unite? Or should we think tactically, asking what the most effective strategy would be to defeat Infantino?” In opposing Infantino, Tashima is going against his own confederation after the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) announced last month that it would support the 56-year-old Swiss for re-election. Infantino also has the backing of the Confederation of African Football (CAF), while South American governing body CONMEBOL is largely supportive. Under his rule, FIFA’s profits have skyrocketed and so have the amounts that member federations receive. item.title: Middle Belt youth leader rejects Tinubu’s 2027 endorsement, backs Obi
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS — The National Youth Leader of the Middle Belt Forum (MBF), Emmanuel Zopmal, has rejected the purported endorsement of President Bola Tinubu for re-election in 2027 by some Middle Belt leaders, declaring support for the presidential ambition of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) candidate, Peter Obi, and his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso. Zopmal, who is also the North-Central Coordinator of The Big-Tent Coalition, stated this on Thursday while addressing journalists in Jos, Plateau State, where he presented the position of the Middle Belt youth leadership on the political future of the region. He faulted the reported endorsement, alleging that it did not reflect the collective position of the people because critical stakeholders, including community leaders, traditional institutions, youths and women, were not consulted before the visit to the President. “There was no due consultation with Middle Belt communities, elders, traditional institutions, youths and women who feel and live the terrible experiences in our various communities before the purported endorsement of President Tinubu for the 2027 re-election bid,” he said. Zopmal described the reported endorsement as insensitive to the security and economic challenges confronting communities across the region and the country. He cited insecurity, economic hardship, inflation, rising borrowings and poverty as issues that should have informed any political position taken in the name of the Middle Belt. The MBF youth leader also questioned the leadership and administrative structure of the forum, alleging that it had operated without a General Assembly, elections, constitutional processes and accountability for eight years. He called for the organisation to return to democratic principles and provide clearer direction for the Middle Belt struggle. He also criticised the immediate past President of the forum, Dr Pogu Bitrus, over what he described as a lack of broad-based consultations in the organisation’s activities. “We believe that no individual or group should assume the authority to speak for the entire Middle Belt without the consent and participation of the people and the various structures of the Forum,” he said. On the recent visit by some Middle Belt leaders to Tinubu, which involved elder statesman and retired General Theophilus Danjuma, Zopmal alleged that the exercise was influenced by the political interests of some individuals. He expressed concern that the outcome of the meeting could be wrongly associated with Danjuma’s position without the wider consent of the people. Zopmal further argued that the Middle Belt Forum should remain non-partisan, questioning why representatives of opposition parties from the region were excluded from the engagement. “Middle Belt Forum is not a partisan platform. item.title: Video: Fresh protest hits South Africa as demonstrators demand ban on Nigerians
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde A fresh anti-Nigerian protest has erupted in South Africa, with demonstrators in Pretoria demanding that the government close its borders to Nigerian nationals and prohibit their entry into the country. The demonstration, organised by the March and March movement on Wednesday, saw protesters accuse Nigerians of involvement in drug trafficking and worsening social problems in South African communities. In a video shared by South African broadcaster, Newzroom Afrika, the group’s leader, Jacinta Ngobese-Zuma, was seen leading demonstrators through Sunnyside, a Pretoria suburb with a sizeable Nigerian population, popularly nicknamed ‘Little Lagos’. Video: Fresh protest hits South Africa as demonstrators demand ban on Nigerians Led by Jacinta Ngobese-Zuma, the protesters say the 1951 Refugee Convention is not sustainable and feasible, and South Africa should get out of it. pic.twitter.com/5nam29TgCL — Vanguard Newspapers (@vanguardngrnews) November 19, 2026 Addressing Nigerians in the neighbourhood, Ngobese-Zuma questioned how the area acquired the nickname and challenged residents to explain their presence in the community. “I am being told here that we’ve entered Sunnyside, the home of Nigerians. I am inviting Nigerians to come out, let’s talk to each other. We want to know who gave you this place and called it Nigeria. Who gave you permission to call this place Lagos or whatever you call it?” she said. She also described the presence of migrants in the country as unsustainable, alleging that they were putting pressure on public resources and contributing to the difficulties faced by South African citizens. The group’s legal representative, Xolani Zuma, also called for a blanket ban on Nigerians entering South Africa, accusing them of selling drugs to South Africans. “The state must ban Nigerians from South Africa. They must ban Nigerians until they stop selling drugs to our people. The rest of Africa, we are fine, but we do not want Nigerians in South Africa anymore. That is what we are saying,” he said. Speaking in another video, Ngobese-Zuma urged the South African government to withdraw from the 1951 United Nations Convention Relating to the Status of Refugees, arguing that its obligations under the agreement were no longer sustainable. “We need to get out of it, it’s not sustainable or feasible,” she said. item.title: Super Eagles must improve or miss 2027 AFCON – Jo Bonfere
item.description: Former Super Eagles coach, Jo Bonfrere, has warned that Nigeria could miss out on the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations if the team fails to improve its performance in the remaining qualifying matches. Bonfrere gave the warning following Nigeria’s goalless draw against Tanzania’s Taifa Stars in Zanzibar on Tuesday, a result he described as a setback to the country’s qualification campaign. The result left the three-time African champions second in Group L with seven points from four matches, three points behind leaders Guinea-Bissau, who defeated Madagascar 2-0 in Bissau. With only group winners guaranteed qualification for the tournament, the former coach said Nigeria must win their remaining fixtures to avoid putting their AFCON hopes in jeopardy. Speaking to Complete Sports, Bonfrere said the Super Eagles missed an opportunity to close the gap on Guinea-Bissau with a victory in Zanzibar. “It’s a poor result for the Super Eagles,” he said. “The Super Eagles should have done better. A win would have bridged the gap with Guinea-Bissau. But with this result, they will have to work hard in their two remaining games or risk seeing their 2027 AFCON ambition fade,” the 80-year-old said. Bonfrere, who led Nigeria’s U-23 team to football gold at the 1996 Olympic Games in Atlanta, Georgia, also expressed concern over the team’s scoring record in the qualifiers. Nigeria have scored five goals and conceded the same number in four Group L matches, a record the Dutch tactician said was below expectations, considering the quality of players available to the country. He argued that the Super Eagles should be scoring more goals, given that several members of the squad feature for top European clubs. “You score goals, you win games. If you don’t score, you don’t win. The Super Eagles have good players in top European teams. They have more experience than any other team in Africa. So, they must score goals,” he said. Comparing Nigeria’s performance with that of Guinea-Bissau, Bonfrere noted that the group leaders had scored eight goals and conceded just one in their four matches. “You said Guinea-Bissau have scored eight goals and conceded one. That’s good for them. That’s what the Super Eagles should be doing, and even more, because Nigeria have quality players,” he added. Nigeria will return to action in March 2027 when they travel to face Madagascar in their Matchday Five encounter, while Guinea-Bissau host Tanzania. The Super Eagles will then conclude their qualifying campaign against Guinea-Bissau at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium, Uyo, on March 28. Both fixtures are crucial to Nigeria’s chances of securing a place at the 2027 AFCON. The post Super Eagles must improve or miss 2027 AFCON – Jo Bonfere appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Unionism not a licence for irresponsibility, Wike’s aide slams UniAbuja staff
item.description: …Says varsity used only 1,426.67 hectares in 38 yrs By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Lere Olayinka, Senior Special Assistant on Public Communications and Social Media to the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory FCT, Nyesom Wike, has told staff of the University of Abuja that “unionism and activism should not be a licence for reckless advertisement of irresponsible behaviour” as they agitate over the reduction of the institution’s land from 11,824.04 hectares to 4,685 hectares. In a statement on Thursday in Abuja, Olayinka described the utterances of the union leaders, especially the chairman of the Academic Staff Union of Universities ASUU at the university, Professor Sylvanus Ugoh, as unbecoming of people operating in an academic environment. Olayinka said after existing for 38 years, the university had used a fraction of its land. “Most importantly, after existing for 38 years, UNIABUJA has only utilized 1,426.67 hectares of land, with 49.56 hectares used for staff quarters. What then is the need for over 11,000 hectares of land when less than 1,500 hectares was utilized in 38 years?” he asked. He dismissed the claim by the Joint Action Committee (JAC), which is seeking a reversal of the reduction, that the Minister forged the 2016 report of the Joint Committee of the Federal Capital Territory Administration (FCTA) and UNIABUJA on Land and Sundry Issues. The committee was set up by the then FCT Minister, Mohamed Musa Bello. Olayinka called the allegation recklessness and irresponsibility taken too far. “It is therefore strange that supposed academia will hide under an unknown Joint Action Committee to insult the person of the FCT Minister and accuse him of forging official documents of the government arising from a committee duly set up by his predecessor,” he said. He added that apart from the 2016 committee, another one was set up on December 17, 2020, following the university management’s visit to the FCT Minister on October 13, 2020. According to him, part of the recommendations of the December 2020 committee read: “Based on the recommended size of 100Ha for a University Campus stipulated by the National University Commission and considering that the University has held the title of about 11,608.33Ha for over thirty (30) years, a total of about 1,922.66Ha should be left to the University while the remaining part of the land should be designed and detailed by URP (Urban and Regional Planning) Department for compatible land use like Institution and Research Districts.” The recommendation went on: “This will solve the issues of continuous and unabated village expansion which will save the FCTA the unending trouble of village encroachments and the cost of removing them.” Olayinka said the issues the university presented to the 2016 committee included the issuance of Certificate of Occupancy for its main and mini campuses and its properties in Kado and Jahi districts. item.title: AI being run in a ‘mediaeval’ way – UN
item.description: Artificial intelligence is being governed in an almost mediaeval fashion, the UN rights chief warned Thursday, with power concentrated in the hands of a few tech barons. Speaking at the RightsX summit in Geneva, Volker Turk said that while the story of AI sounded futuristic, underneath it was an age-old narrative of power. “A handful of men still control much of the world’s AI computing power, data and infrastructure. And we still have no common rules to pace or steer AI development,” he said. Turk said there was a glaring democratic deficit when five technology companies owned more than 70 percent of global AI computing capacity. “We have the technology of the future governed in an almost mediaeval way: by a select few, with virtually no checks, no balances, no participation, and no accountability,” he said. “History has taught us: with this kind of power, the rights and freedoms of ordinary people are the first to suffer.” Reiterating his call for rights-centred AI regulation, the UN high commissioner for human rights said the technology was increasingly controlling people’s lives. And this, he warned, was often happening without their knowledge, and could distort public debate in “subtle, insidious ways”. Meanwhile biased algorithms could reproduce injustice on an industrial scale, he cautioned. – ‘Civilisational collapse’ – “Our transport, food and healthcare are increasingly digitised. We may not be far from the day when AI can cut off the critical infrastructure of entire communities or countries, either on its own or in the wrong hands,” Turk warned. “When people discuss the chances of civilisational collapse because of AI, we need to ask: who decides what chances we take?” He voiced optimism that people would ultimately challenge unchecked power, with the democratic deficit turning into a deficit of trust. He cited young people already stepping offline to regain greater control of their lives. Turk said AI’s benefits should be shared equitably, which would require goodwill from technology companies, but also regulation and accountability. He said he had written to frontier AI companies urging them to introduce effective safeguards “before it is too late”. Turk noted that a bottle of milk could not make it to a shop without layers of testing, rules and regulations. So for AI, “it’s a no-brainer that you need some form of regulation”, given its potential for harm, Turk said. As for how models are trained, he suggested giving the Universal Declaration of Human Rights “as the task to AI”. The post AI being run in a ‘mediaeval’ way – UN appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: ‘No more playstation’ – Anthony Joshua welcomes baby girl
item.description: Nigerian-British boxing champion, Anthony Joshua, has announced the birth of his second child, a girl, noting that there is no more time for PlayStation or FIFA for him. Joshua and his childhood sweetheart, Nicole Osbourne, welcomed their daughter on November 14, 2026. The pair also have an 11-year-old son, Joseph. The former two-time unified heavyweight champion revealed this in an interview with The Sun , which gained attention on Thursday, said having a daughter would help him better understand women and how to support them. “Now I’ve got a daughter, I will get an insight and a bit more understanding of what it means to be a woman, and how I can be supportive. My daughter will give me firsthand experience of a woman’s power,” he said. Joshua disclosed that the family had yet to settle on a name for the newborn, but described her as his princess. “I’ve spoken to all the women in my family, and it’s amazing the amount of support that women give each other. We haven’t given her a name yet, but she’s my Princess,” he added. The 36 year old boxer described the birth as a huge blessing, revealing that he deliberately avoided finding out the baby’s sex during the pregnancy. “It’s been amazing, a big blessing and I can’t believe I’m a girl dad. I didn’t want to find the sex out during the pregnancy,” Joshua said. He also joked about how having a daughter could change some of the activities he shares with his son. “I love boys but as soon as I found out we had a little girl I said, ‘No more Fifa, no more motorbiking, no more PlayStation!’” he said. “I’m going to do it all, so you might see me with some eyeshadow on, some nail polish on, drinking some tea in a doll’s playhouse and just trying to do the right thing by her, you know?” he said. He also spoke about the responsibilities of caring for a newborn, saying he was prepared to change nappies and go through the demands of raising a baby again. “I will change nappies, I’ve gotta go through all that stinky bum time again!” he added. The development comes as Joshua prepares for a reported December 11 showdown with fellow British heavyweight boxer Tyson Fury. item.title: Oil resumption: KAGOTE insists Ogoni people must ratify FG’s MoU
item.description: …Group welcomes Tinubu’s intervention on Eleme section of East-West Road By Daniel Abia, Port Harcourt The leadership of KAGOTE, comprising Khana, Gokana, Tai and Eleme local government areas of Rivers State, has insisted that the proposed Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between the Federal Government and the Ogoni people on the resumption of oil exploration in Ogoniland must be ratified by the people before it is signed. The group said the contents of the proposed agreement must be presented to the Ogoni people for approval to secure their mandate and ensure the legitimacy of the process. KAGOTE President, Chief Lesi Ma-ol, stated this in a statement, explaining that it had been agreed that congresses should be convened in Khana, Gokana, Tai and Eleme by their duly elected local government chairmen to consider and ratify the proposed agreement. He said the arrangement would address concerns over the legality and legitimacy of the Ogoni Dialogue Committee (ODC) and provide a platform for the people to approve the MoU with the Federal Government. Ma-ol stressed the need for unity within the ODC, insisting that no individual or group of members should sign any agreement on behalf of the committee without its collective approval and ratification by the congresses. “We consider the unity of the ODC as essential, as such it was resolved that we shall sign as a collective. No member or group of members shall, by themselves, sign any document on behalf of the ODC that has not been adopted by the ODC and approved/ratified by the congresses. “We are totally in support of the resumption of oil and gas exploration in Ogoniland. We are committed to ensuring that the necessary foundations are properly laid. We want a resumption that brings peace, security, employment, economic opportunities, environmental responsibility and sustainable development to our land,” he said. The KAGOTE president said President Bola Tinubu initiated the peace process with good intentions, adding that the group was committed to doing everything possible to ensure its success. He, however, said a sustainable outcome must be built on trust, inclusiveness, transparency and the legitimate mandate of the Ogoni people. Ma-ol explained that KAGOTE was currently involved in harmonising the Federal Government’s response to the demands of the Ogoni people, a process expected to culminate in the proposed MoU. item.title: Mera denies defection rumour to APC in Kebbi
item.description: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi The African Democratic Congress (ADC) senatorial candidate for Kebbi North, Alhaji Ibrahim Muhammad Mera, has dismissed reports circulating on social media that he has defected to the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) in Kebbi State. Mera, in a statement signed by his Director-General, Media, Garba Muhammad Yeldu, on Thursday, said he had neither met nor held discussions with any APC official or member over a possible defection. He described the reports as fabricated, alleging that they were being circulated by individuals seeking to create confusion and distract him from pursuing his senatorial ambition under the ADC. Mera acknowledged that political parties were experiencing internal challenges but insisted that the crisis within the ADC would not make him abandon the party. He said the APC also had its internal disagreements, adding that he remained focused on his political ambition and the pursuit of the Kebbi North senatorial seat. The ADC candidate urged his supporters and constituents to disregard the reports, describing them as products of the rumour peddlers’ imagination. He also appealed to them to remain calm, peaceful and law-abiding while continuing to support the ADC. “I have never for once thought or made attempts to leave ADC. I remain focused and unrelenting in the pursuit of my mandate in my party,” he said. Mera warned those behind the reports to desist from spreading what he described as false information and assured his supporters of his continued loyalty to the ADC. item.title: ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ Launches Worldwide To Near-Perfect Reviews
item.description: Gamers around the world got their first taste of “Grand Theft Auto VI” on Wednesday, as critics heaped praise on one of the most anticipated video game releases ever. The latest installment of the crime franchise comes 13 years after the last full edition broke sales records and became one of the most profitable entertainment products of all time. The series lets players live out gangster fantasies, smash up cars and fight whoever they choose in a fictionalized US city populated by lowlifes, sex workers and thugs. “GTA VI” launched first in New Zealand at midnight local time (1100 GMT Wednesday) and is rolling out around the world as each market reaches midnight. New Zealander Luke Starik was among the first to play, and his character did not last long. “Wasted already. First one, didn’t survive long,” he told AFP, laughing. “This is one of the big things in my life…I’ve been playing GTA for such a long time,” Riley Fennel, an Australian student visiting Tokyo, told AFP. Review aggregator Metacritic gave the game a score of 99 out of 100. A 42-year-old gamer wrote on a German-language Reddit forum that he had taken time off work to play all night. By 1:20 am, he was already in bed with a headache, still blown away by the game. “Thirteen years ago, with a game like this, I’d have played until six in the morning,” the gamer wrote. In the game’s official Reddit forum, people raved about improved interactive elements, such as being able to push a stranded ski jet back in the water. “This is amazing!” one person wrote. Analytics firm Omdia estimates “GTA VI” could generate $3.2 billion in sales by the end of the year for studio Rockstar Games and parent company Take-Two Interactive. PlayStation briefly reported connection issues on its status page before services were restored. People play Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI) at Bamboo Gaming Center & Bar in Bangkok on November 19, 2026, on the day of the highly anticipated video game’s release. Photo by LILLIAN SUWANRUMPHA / AFP ‘Taylor Swift of games’ In a review for The Verge titled “GTA VI does something impossible — it lives up to the hype,” Andrew Webster wrote that “the game is so good that the outsize hype is the least interesting thing about it.” Social media users praised the graphics. “There’s one moment, no spoilers, where the light hits behind one of the characters just right, and I swore I was looking at a real human,” wrote Reddit user No_Strike9652. Before the release, Joost van Dreunen, a professor at New York University’s Stern School of Business, told AFP the game was an “outlier” in the entertainment industry. “This is the Taylor Swift of video games,” he said. “The reach of the game is such that it will lead to a downstream effect on engagement on other entertainment services,” such as streaming platforms, said Omdia analyst James McWhirter. item.title: I Will Rejoin Military To Fight Russia If Needed — Prince Harry
item.description: Britain’s Prince Harry said he would “sign up again” to serve in the military and fight against Russia if needed, in an interview from Ukraine with The Telegraph aired Thursday. “I think there’s a lot that the whole world can learn from Ukraine,” the prince said during an unannounced visit to the western city of Lviv over the weekend. “If asked to sign up again, if the need is there, then I will 100% be there to serve my country alongside my fellow veterans and service personnel.” Britain’s Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex, speaks during the closing ceremony of the Ukrainian Invictus Games in Lviv, on November 15, 2026. Harry, a former British army officer and the younger son of King Charles III, made his fourth visit to Ukraine since Russia’s 2022 invasion to meet wounded veterans and medics. The prince is also the founder of the Invictus Games for wounded veterans and met athletes hoping to represent Ukraine at next year’s games in the British city of Birmingham. “Just because there’s not drones, bullets, and rockets flying at us, that doesn’t mean that we’re not at war,” he told the British daily’s “Ukraine: The Latest” podcast. “I feel very confident that Europe has a united front, and it would be fantastic to have more American support for that as well,” he added. Britain’s Prince Harry, Duke of Sussex (C) poses for photos with Ukrainian war veterans during the Ukrainian Invictus Games in Lviv, on November 15, 2026. Earlier on his weekend visit to Lviv, he told wounded veterans and medics specialising in war injuries: “You’re going to win the war”. He repeated that sentiment on the podcast, insisting that “Ukraine are winning” and “there is no version where Russia is making any more advances”. The 42-year-old prince has previously spoken about being moved by witnessing death and life-changing injuries while on deployment in Afghanistan, and launched the Invictus Games in 2014 when he was still in the British army. Harry, his wife Meghan and their two children moved back to the UK earlier this year from California amid an enduring rift with the royal family and his brother and heir-to-the-throne Prince William. But the Sussex couple have launched themselves back into public life since their surprise return, carrying out engagements and visiting the EU parliament last week for an event about the dangers children face online. Despite their busy schedule, Meghan has been keeping a relatively low profile since her estranged father was charged in the US for the alleged possession of child sexual abuse images. item.title: South Koreans Sit Key College Exam Mired In Cheating Scandal
item.description: South Korea cut Wi-Fi around exam halls and is offering $75,000 rewards to whistleblowers in an all-out battle against AI-assisted cheating as half a million students sit their gruelling college entrance exams on Thursday. Known as the Suneung, the once-a-year, nine-hour-long exam is widely seen as a ticket to prestigious universities, well-paid jobs, and even better marriage prospects in the highly competitive country. But this year, fears of AI-assisted cheating have driven authorities to extraordinary lengths, including doubling the number of supervisors and sending random emergency alerts to detect any smartphones illegally smuggled into the exam centres. As students were still taking the test on Thursday afternoon, South Korea’s Prime Minister Han Seong-sook ordered that Suneung papers from 2025 be kept for a cheating probe. “The Ministry of Education shall maintain the current storage conditions of last year’s (college entrance exam) papers until further notice,” the PM’s office said, adding that they are normally discarded after the following year’s test. Anxious parents were earlier seen hugging their children in the South Korean capital, where temperatures dropped below zero overnight. “I came here with a heavy heart because of concerns over AI cheating,” Bang Min-ji, 18, told AFP as she prepared to enter the Yeouido Girls’ High School in central Seoul on Thursday morning. The exam kicked off at 8.40 am (2340 GMT Wednesday), with a nationwide mobile phone alert sounding 10 minutes beforehand. An AFP photographer saw a late-running student race into the high school after getting a ride in a police car. Students were told to turn up with just pencils. Erasers will be provided by the test centres, as authorities try to reduce the chances of concealed digital devices disguised as stationery. Exam-takers were also asked to avoid wearing clothes with buttons, with those who fail to comply having stickers placed over the buttons to prevent the use of hidden cameras. Bang said she feared that restrictions on writing instruments could disrupt her exam. “I’m worried I might panic if I have difficulty using the stationery provided during the test.” Elsewhere in the South Korean capital, boys were pictured with their heads in their hands as they sat nervously at exam desks. A total of 22 test-takers were found with smartphones after the morning alerts were sent, vice education minister Choi Eun-ok told a press briefing. They would be referred to exam authorities to undergo “a thorough inspection to determine whether they were carrying miniature cameras or other electronic devices”, she said.
